minutes.headline: Open Space Committee reviewed town land titles, a state boat-access offer at Lake Shirley, and the trails and hunting rules.
minutes.summary: The committee reviewed ownership and deed history for several town parcels and heard that state Fisheries and Wildlife is interested in building a free public boat access on Lake Shirley if the town can prove it owns the land. A member presented a deed-by-deed review of conservation land, with an action plan to fix records and transfers. Updates followed on trail maps and the hunting debate in the land use rules. Only the January minutes and adjournment were voted.

budget_items.topic: Fisheries and Wildlife boat access at Lake Shirley
budget_items.what_was_said: The state would do the engineering and build parking, racks and docks at no cost to the town if the town shows it owns the land, and the town would maintain it.
A member suggested a nominal fee could fund a boat greeter and maintenance, though the state agreement may restrict this.
Members noted the property-of-low-value taking process has costs for filing and recording, and a past board set aside a budget share for takings.
A member read the deed showing the transfer to the town, dated 1997.

what_happened.line: The Open Space Committee held no votes on land, money or policy; it voted only on the January minutes and adjournment.
The committee heard that state Fisheries and Wildlife would build a free public boat access at Lake Shirley if the town can show it owns the land.
A member presented a deed-by-deed review of conservation land, and members agreed to search town meeting records for missing conservation transfers.
Members assigned follow-ups: a list of Lake Shirley properties to go to the state contact, and more research on the Woodruff and Pleasant Street parcels.
The committee set its next meeting for March 16, 2021, at 6:30.

why_it_matters: A state-built boat access at Lake Shirley would cost the town nothing to build, but the town would maintain it, and the offer depends on the town proving it holds title to the land.
Gaps in the records of conservation land transfers affect which parcels the town can show it owns, and so what it can protect, build on or accept state help for.
watch_next: The March 16, 2021 meeting, where the agenda is to include the Oliver lot, the purple-flagged parcels and a Lake Shirley parcel list.
Whether the town can document ownership of the Lake Shirley parcels, which the state boat-access offer depends on.
